\subsection*{Light --- Assigns: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Programs.Light.Assigns}.

\subsection*{Light --- Assigns: Results}

\begin{definition}[Assigned variables of a statement]
\lean{Light.Stmt.assigns}
\label{Light.Stmt.assigns}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Stmt}
For a statement built from the given syntax, define its assigned-variable list
recursively as follows: a skip or a store has the empty list; an assignment to variable
$x$ or a procedure call storing its result in $x$ has list $[x]$; sequential composition
and conditionals concatenate the lists of their two branches; and a while loop has the
list of its body.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unchanged unassigned locations]
\lean{Light.Exec.loc_eq_of_notMem_assigns}
\label{Light.Exec.loc_eq_of_notMem_assigns}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Exec, Light.State, Light.Stmt, Light.Stmt.assigns}
\difficulty{5}
Fix resource limits and a program. For any imperative statement, states $\sigma$ and
$\sigma'$, cost $c$, and natural-number variable index $y$, if the statement executes
from $\sigma$ to $\sigma'$ with cost $c$ and $y$ does not occur in its assigned-variable
list, then $\sigma'.loc(y)=\sigma.loc(y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of unassigned locals]
\lean{Light.Ends.keeping}
\label{Light.Ends.keeping}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Exec.loc_eq_of_notMem_assigns, Light.State, Light.Stmt, Light.Stmt.assigns}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. If a statement $s$ can
execute from state $\sigma$ with cost at most $T$ to a state satisfying $Q$, then it can
execute with the same cost bound to a state satisfying $Q$ in which every local variable
not assigned by $s$ has the same value as in $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation outside a chosen local set]
\lean{Light.Ends.keepingBut}
\label{Light.Ends.keepingBut}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Ends, Light.Ends.keeping, Light.Ends.mono, Light.State, Light.Stmt, Light.Stmt.assigns}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. Let $s$ be a statement,
$X$ a list of local indices containing every local assigned by $s$, and $\sigma$ an
initial state. If $s$ can execute from $\sigma$ with cost at most $T$ to a state
satisfying $Q$, then it can execute with the same cost bound to a state satisfying $Q$
in which every local index outside $X$ has the same value as in $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}
